                   I.       INTRODUCTION AND SUMMARY OF POSITION

        The Covert’s and Maddox’s interests and concerns in this proceeding are the same – the

significant and detrimental impact on their ranches resulting from the construction and permanent

placement of a 765kV transmission line. The real world impacts will effect certain habitable

         III.   THE PUC SHOULD AVOID USE OF LINKS J33, J6, AND K41
                                FOR ANY ROUTE

         Covert and Maddox request that the ALJs recommend a proposed route that does not

include Links J33, J6, and K41. 41 These links will only be used to move the transmission line to

the most southern corridor of this project and will directly impact these two sets of landowners, as

well as many other landowners and property along these links. Use of these links and the general

shift to the most southern corridor will increase the length and costs compared to Route 894 and

will negatively impact the environmental integrity, aesthetics, ranching operations, and the

watersheds. The shift is unnecessary as the Applicants’ Best-Meets Route 894 and the PUC Staff’s

best Route 487 meet the statutory and regulatory requirements for approving a transmission line

route.

Maddox submit that use of these three Links in any route should be rejected for use in the final

recommended route for this project.

       A. Failures of Links J33, J6, and K41

           Rule § 25.101(b)(3)(B) states the “the line must be routed to the extent reasonable to

moderate the impact on the affected community and landowners unless grid reliability and security

dictate otherwise.”(emphasis added). The Applicants have not claimed that grid reliability or

security issues exist and, therefore, the general policy of moderating the impact on landowners, as

well as the community is mandated; it is not optional. Landowners know their land and the

ecosystem of the area. This knowledge is not based on empirical data or mathematical formula –

it is based on real life experiences and living and working on that land. Use of these links will

impact their properties in ways that will be generational damage.

         Covert and Maddox submit that there are at least six reasons that Links J33, J6, and K41,

individually and collectively, should not be used in any route recommended by the ALJs or

approved by the PUC.

        Fragmentation and Failure of Paralleling Exercise. As a general policy, the PUC seeks to

minimize or to avoid links that bisect property and the environment. To follow the PURA and

regulatory factors, the transmission line should seek to follow existing rights-of-way, property

lines and areas that have been previously disturbed. 43 Failure to do so and to fragment or divide

land that has not been “disturbed” (e.g., current easement, rights-of-way, transmission line, or

property line) would not be in compliance with PURA or the PUC Rules.44 The use of paralleling

is recognized as factor in considering a particular route, which would include use of existing rights-

of-way, easements, transmission lines, or property boundaries. 45 And, admittedly in a project this

size, there will be fragmentation of properties that are sliced by the 200-foot wide easement and

tower structures. But that does not mean that the ALJs or the PUC should not consider significant

fragmentation of undisturbed property, which is what will happen to the Covert ranches through

use of Links J6 or K41.

Covert ranches. Based on the Oncor Intervenor Map, Links J33, J6 and K41 would cut the Covert
